name: New Zealand

outcome.intro: After studying this section, a student will know the general location, climate, and style of wine produced in New Zealand's most important wine regions.
outcome.certified: After studying this section, a candidate will know the specific locations, climates, and principal grape varieties of New Zealand's most important wine regions. A Certified Sommelier will have the ability to describe New Zealand Sauvignon Blanc, the natural factors that are responsible for its distinct style, and be able to recommend and sell food pairings with New Zealand wines to a guest.

rows.intro: Southern Hemisphere; Two islands: North Island and South Island; 4,100 km/2,500 miles to the southeast of Australia.
South Island: Cool; Marlborough: Cool maritime (with protection); Central Otago: Cool continental; North Island: Warmer, humid; Hawke's Bay: Moderate maritime
rows.certified: Gisborne: Cool maritime; Wairarapa: Cool maritime

rows.intro: Geographical Indications (GIs): trademark only with no minimums, no rules.; New Zealand GI; North Island GI:; Hawke's Bay GI; Gimblett Gravels; South Island GI:; Marlborough GI; Central Otago GI
rows.certified: North Island GI:; Gisborne GI; Wairarapa GI; Martinborough GI; South Island GI:; Marlborough GI:; Labeling requires 100% fruit from the region.; Subregions:; Awatere Valley; Wairau Valley; Nelson GI; Canterbury GI

rows.intro: South Island: Long sunlight hours; North Island: Humidity
Clean, modern, winemaking, use of screwcaps.
Pinot Noir, Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, Merlot
85% min to list the grape variety on a label.
Whites: Typically unoaked, high flavor intensity with high natural acidity.; Reds: Lightly oaked

rows.certified: Cloudy Bay, Felton Road, Villa Maria
Recent vintages are 6 months ahead of Northern Hemisphere.

rows.intro: Young industry, temperance movement, innovation, screwcap initiative.
rows.certified: Know Scott Henry and Vertical Shoot Position (VSP) trellis systems.
Know how to open a screwcap.

rows.intro: High-acid and unoaked wines with seafood, starters, salads. Intense flavors can be too much for super delicate dishes.
rows.certified: Sauvignon Blanc has ripeness for sweet-savory ingredients (e.g., mango salsa); pair acid with acid. Pinot Noir and Bordeaux blends can be elegant non-European options.
